notes: A standalone AD compliance report, built to be handed to an owner or filed with the aircraft records. It leads with what is outstanding rather than burying it: a count band, then a red statement naming the number of directives not complied with and what 91.403(a) says about that, then the recurring ones with their next-due dates, then the record grouped by the product each directive was issued against. Every line carries the subject and, where the index has it, the applicability wording, so the page can be checked instead of trusted. One signature block at the end. Green complied, amber due or to verify, red outstanding — the same colours the rest of the paperwork uses, and not brandable.
validated_against: The FAA's own model search on drs.faa.gov, 23 models, Status=Current: 693 directives listed, 693 returned, 0 wrongly set aside. Perfect on every individual model. AD Toolbox's airframe lists hold 528 of the same 693 — mostly by design, since their appliance directives sit in a separate unmatched list of 581.
reliability: 40 aircraft configurations searched end to end: 0 page errors, 0 problems. 167 self checks passing. Full entries to read across the 40 fell from 3,847 to 2,036, with 1,811 kept as one-line rows.

index.source: FAA Dynamic Regulatory System, AD Final Rules

fix: The method-of-compliance picker was built wrong and a mechanic said so within a day of getting it. It was one dropdown of twenty-five whole sentences: the list truncated at 78 characters so you could not read the option you were choosing, and sixteen of the wordings carried "____" for a serial or a date, so choosing one meant hunting through the sentence to type in a blank. Faster to type it yourself, which is the definition of a feature that failed. Rebuilt as two short choices — what the answer is, then why — with the sentence composing itself underneath where it can be read and edited. Nothing in either list exceeds 24 characters, and no wording contains a blank: every value comes from the aeroplane or from a field that already exists on the row.
storage: The directive index no longer shares a database with jobs and photographs. It lives in Cache Storage under 'adx-1'. Any copy left in the old place is deleted on first load. This is the second half of the 30 August fix: the database that wedged that morning is now smaller and is never touched by an AD search.
